text: In EXP-002 all 48 primary contrasts (2 social rules x 24 cells) are positive and Holm-significant at familywise 0.05 (Holm family m = 48, no degenerate contrast; largest Holm-adjusted p 3.1e-14); H1 supported.
scope: N=50, own-signal ties, q in {0.55,0.60,0.70,0.80}, networks complete/window-2/window-3, v in {1,0.5}; synthetic agents only
limitations: Model-bound; magnitudes, not p-values, carry the message; two contrasts are convention-dependent (CLM-005)

text: Effect sizes in EXP-002 range from +0.0059 on the proportion scale, 0.59 accuracy points (imitation, q=0.55, window-2, v=0.5; 95% CI [0.0048, 0.0070]) to +0.1439 (imitation, q=0.70, window-3, v=1; 95% CI [0.1375, 0.1504]).
The pre-stated expectation that naive imitation lowers accuracy in some window-k cell at low q is contradicted: imitation is significantly positive in every EXP-002 cell.
scope: as CLM-001; one simple naive rule (vote counting)
limitations: Other imitation rules or heterogeneous populations may behave differently

text: Under the complete network with own-signal ties, Bayesian and imitation actions are identical on every episode (C4: 0 differing episodes in all 8 EXP-002 complete cells, 10,000 episodes each), as pre-stated.
limitations: Structural prediction of the model, not an empirical finding about people

text: Under coin-flip ties (EXP-003 V1), the EXP-002 contrasts at q=0.55, window-3, v=1 lose Holm significance (Bayesian Delta 0.0082, 95% CI [-0.0013, 0.0176]; imitation 0.0079, [-0.0015, 0.0174]; Holm p 0.18); by the frozen rule these two EXP-002 conclusions are convention-dependent.
limitations: Loss of significance is not evidence of a zero effect

text: Of the 72 EXP-003 robustness comparisons (24 EXP-002 contrasts x 3 variations), 70 keep sign and Holm significance and none reverses sign.
scope: EXP-003 grid only; q=0.60 and 0.80 untested for robustness
limitations: Rule tracks sign and significance, not magnitude

text: Coin-flip ties reduce every social-learning gain in the EXP-003 grid (all 24 V1 contrasts below their EXP-002 values; by more than half in 16 of 24).
limitations: No planned test of the difference between variations

text: Social learning coexists with frequent cascades of errors: in EXP-002 wrong-cascade probabilities of the social rules reach 0.87 (imitation, q=0.55, window-3, v=0.5) and the mean longest wrong run of Bayesian agents at q=0.55, v=1 is about 20 of 50 agents against about 4.4 for the baseline.
limitations: Secondary metric; wrong-cascade counts an episode once even if the cascade breaks later

text: Exploratory: in the window networks, imitation's gain exceeds the Bayesian gain under window-3 with v=1 (by 0.002 to 0.010 on the proportion scale) and falls below it with v=0.5 (by 0.003 to 0.018).
limitations: No planned imitation-versus-Bayesian test; candidate for a new preregistered experiment; superseded in detail by the paired intervals of CLM-013 (M4)

text: Exploratory: at q in {0.60, 0.80}, the 72 EXP-003-type comparisons (V1 coin ties, V2 N=10, V3 N=200) are all robust (same sign, Holm-significant); coin ties reduce the gains to 0.27 to 0.63 of their EXP-002 values.
limitations: Post hoc; does not change the confirmatory EXP-003 verdict

text: Exploratory: in EXP-002 a social rule ends below the independent baseline on the same episode in 0.050 to 0.425 of episodes (0.371 to 0.425 at q=0.55); with v=1 this share equals the wrong-cascade probability to three decimals.
Exploratory: the last agent's paired accuracy gain is positive in all 48 EXP-002 contrasts (0.0067 to 0.1595), with 95% intervals excluding zero.
limitations: Unadjusted intervals; addresses the averaging confounder for sign only

text: Exploratory: paired imitation-minus-Bayesian differences: negative in all 8 half-visibility window cells (-0.0032 to -0.0178), positive in 3 of 4 window-3 v=1 cells (0.0052 to 0.0104), zero on every episode in the 4 window-2 v=1 cells.
limitations: No multiplicity control; candidate for a preregistered test

text: 46 of the 48 EXP-002 contrasts exceed the protocol's practical threshold of 0.01; the 2 below it (imitation +0.0059, Bayesian +0.0091, both q=0.55, window-2, v=0.5) are Holm-significant but below the smallest effect the protocol treats as practically meaningful.
limitations: The threshold was stated in the sample-size rationale, not as a decision rule

text: Within the window cells, the Bayesian gain increases with the mean expected number of observed actions at every q, but the Bayesian gain of the complete network (24.50 expected observed actions at v=1) differs from that of window-3 at v=1 (2.88) by less than 0.005 at every q.
limitations: Quantity and structure are confounded in this grid
